audit_findings.title: FY2025 owner earnings may use cash-paid capex instead of economic capex incurred
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.265 million difference between $26.9 million incurred capex and $22.635 million cash purchases, equal to 21.6% of the $19.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: The capital charge directly reduces anchor owner earnings and therefore every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Our total capital expenditures for 2025 were $26.9 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The cash-timing mismatch is demonstrated: the anchor approximately reconciles to net income plus depreciation less the cash-flow-statement purchase figure, while filed capex incurred was $26.9 million and unpaid property-and-equipment purchases increased by $4.415 million. The precise correction remains unresolved because maintenance, growth, remodel, and corporate-office expenditures have not been separated, but the mismatch is large enough to materially affect the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile capital additions, cash payments, and the change in unpaid purchases; classify maintenance versus growth and corporate expenditures; then rerun all scenarios using a normalized economic maintenance-capital charge.

audit_findings.title: The perpetual anchor contains a 53rd operating week
audit_findings.magnitude: At most $1.0 million pre-tax before additional-week G&A and tax effects, or 5.1% of the $19.7 million anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: An extra week temporarily increases FY2025 owner earnings but is capitalized through the forecast and terminal value if the anchor is left unnormalized.
audit_findings.evidence: Fiscal 2025 was a 53-week fiscal year, and fiscal 2024 and 2023 were 52-week fiscal years.
audit_findings.explanation: The 53rd week is demonstrated. The filing attributes $5.8 million of revenue and at least $4.8 million of specified operating expenses to it, leaving no more than $1.0 million before additional-week G&A, the filed $0.1 million tax effect, capital spending, and working-capital effects. That scale cannot bridge the substantial gap between the $6.97-$10.09 scenario values and the $15.37 market price.
audit_findings.action: Prepare a 52-week normalization of revenue, operating costs, working capital, and maintenance capital, and rerun the anchor for precision.

audit_findings.title: All reported cash is treated as excess without establishing that it is distributable
audit_findings.magnitude: At least $7.6 million, or $0.24 per diluted share, is obligation-backed; removing the full $13.282 million would reduce value by $0.42 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Non-excess cash is incorrectly added in the equity bridge even though it supports operations or offsets current obligations.
audit_findings.evidence: Our primary requirements for liquidity and capital are new restaurants, existing restaurant capital investments (remodels and maintenance),lease obligations, interest payments on our debt, working capital and general corporate needs .
audit_findings.explanation: The latest filing demonstrates that $7.6 million of the cash received from a legal settlement belongs to franchisees and was expected to be disbursed, so that portion is not excess cash. Minimum operating cash remains unresolved. Even removing the entire $13.282 million bridge addition would lower the bull value only from $10.09 to approximately $9.67 per share, still well below the $15.37 market price, so it does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the $7.6 million franchisee payable, establish minimum operating and restricted cash from daily liquidity requirements, and rerun the bridge with only demonstrably distributable cash.

audit_findings.title: A nonrecurring legal-settlement gain may remain in the anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: $0.882 million pre-tax; approximately $0.622 million after tax using the filed 29.5% effective rate, equal to 3.2% of the anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained in net income, the one-time settlement increases anchor owner earnings and is capitalized through forecast cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: Includes $0.9 million received from legal settlements, net of legal expenses.
audit_findings.explanation: The filed settlement gain is nonrecurring, and the anchor's approximate reconciliation to GAAP net income indicates that it may have been retained. Removing an estimated $0.622 million after tax would reduce scenario values by roughly $0.21-$0.31 per share, which cannot close the gap to the $15.37 market price or alter the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Inspect the FY2025 owner-earnings worksheet, remove the actual after-tax settlement amount if retained, apply the same normalization policy to genuine nonrecurring expenses, and rerun the scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Workers’ compensation reserves are a material estimation-sensitive claim
audit_findings.mechanism: Reserve inadequacy would create additional claim expense and cash payments, reducing future owner earnings; reserve excess could produce releases with the opposite effect.
audit_findings.evidence: As discussed in Note 2 to the consolidated financial statements, the Company accrued $10.3 million of workers’ compensation reserves in accrued insurance as of December 31, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The $10.3 million workers’ compensation reserve is already recognized, and designation as a critical audit matter demonstrates estimation sensitivity rather than a valuation error. The latest 10-Q reports aggregate accrued insurance of $11.375 million and lower first-half insurance and workers’ compensation expense, but does not disclose the workers’ compensation reserve or an actuarial range. The record therefore does not demonstrate current under-reserving or quantify any adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the actuarial reasonable range, loss-development triangles, subsequent payments, and the July 2026 workers’ compensation reserve; rerun only if those records demonstrate a reserve deficiency or excess.

audit_findings.title: Assigned-lease guarantees create an unmodeled contingent senior claim
audit_findings.magnitude: Unquantified expected loss; latest filed maximum is $11.5 million undiscounted and $9.2 million present value, or $0.29 per diluted share
audit_findings.mechanism: A probability-weighted expected guarantee shortfall would reduce the equity bridge, while actual payments would reduce future owner earnings or cash.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 31, 2025, the potential amount of undiscounted payments the Company could be required to make in the event of non-payment by the primary lessees was $ 3.6 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees are existing contingent claims, but no franchisee default or probable payment is established, and indemnification and cross-default provisions mitigate expected loss. The latest 10-Q increases the gross exposure from the finding's $3.6 million to $11.5 million, with a filed present value of $9.2 million. Even deducting that entire present value would reduce base equity by only 3.2% and value by about $0.29 per share, insufficient to change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the bridge-date guarantees, primary lessee credit quality, sublease coverage, indemnification recoverability, and any defaults; recognize only the resulting probability-weighted expected shortfall.
